newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia sells HRK100 mln 91-day T-bills, price up.
newsitem.headline: Croatia sells HRK100 mln 91-day T-bills, price up.

text.p: Croatia's Finance Ministry raised 100 million kuna through a fresh issue of 91-day treasury bills, priced slightly higher than the last issue at 97.343 percent, it said in a statement.

Thanks to strong investor interest it was able to cut the interest rate further to 10.95 percent, from 11.50 when the treasury's longest maturity paper was last auctioned three weeks ago. For full details see page MFHT.
Bids totalled 137.4 million kuna, more than double the targeted amount, the ministry said. The entire issue went to the banking sector.
Bills are payable on May 2 and mature on July 31.
The Ministry set the next auction for May 13, when it will offer 120 million kuna in 42-day T-bills. Foreign investors can participate indirectly by bidding through local banks.
